issue.title: Release sase-core v0.17.0 and bump the sase-core-rs pin
issue.description:
Epic sase-bg landed the Rust core `task` type and `ready` status in sase-core commit 2e3ff72 (feat(bead)!: add task beads and ready workflow), but that commit is UNRELEASED: the newest sase-core release is v0.16.0 (fe3051b) and release-plz PR sase-org/sase-core#65 (chore: release v0.17.0) is still open.

This repo pins `sase-core-rs>=0.16.0,<0.17.0` (pyproject.toml:46), so any install that resolves the published wheel gets a core with no `task` type and no `ready` status. `sase bead create -T task`, `sase bead update -s ready`, `sase bead ready`, the TaskTriage gate, and the bead_task_triage chop therefore only work in dev workspaces, which build sase_core_rs from the linked checkout (Justfile:22-24). tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version only checks that the pinned minimum exists on PyPI, not that it carries the feature, so `just check` stays green and hides this.

Follow-up:
1. Merge sase-org/sase-core#65 (tags v0.17.0, creates the GitHub release, publishes wheels to PyPI).
2. After the PyPI publish lands, bump pyproject.toml:46 to `sase-core-rs>=0.17.0,<0.18.0` in this repo.

Discovered while landing epic sase-bg. The land agent deliberately did not merge the release PR: publishing to PyPI is outward-facing and irreversible, so it belongs to the project owner.

fields.notes:
SEVERITY ESCALATED (land agent, post-close verification): this is no longer a latent packaging gap — it is an active breakage of the installed sase CLI.

The uv tool env at ~/.local/share/uv/tools/sase carries the PUBLISHED sase_core_rs 0.16.0 wheel, whose event-stream deserializer rejects 'task': every bead read now fails with

  ValueError: validation: invalid bead event stream .../events/streams/sase-bh.jsonl line 1: unknown variant `task`, expected `plan` or `phase`

Because task beads sase-bh and sase-bi are committed to the shared bead store, 'sase bead show/list/ready' all fail for that install, and 'sase commit' silently skips its bead steps (observed on commits 889ddca89 and plans 99b45f5d: 'Bead close failed' + 'Could not publish committed bead pages'). Failure is hard, not graceful degradation.

Version metadata cannot distinguish the two cores: the workspace .venv holds an EDITABLE build from sase/repos/linked/sase-core that also reports 0.16.0 but does support task, which is why just check/just test stay green while the installed CLI is broken. Any feature detection must probe behavior, not the version string.

Unblock options: (1) merge sase-org/sase-core#65 to publish v0.17.0, then bump the pin here (the intended fix); or (2) as a stopgap, reinstall the tool env's sase_core_rs from a locally built dev wheel.

payload.entry: Verified sase-core PR #65 is merged; GitHub release v0.17.0 is published; PyPI serves non-yanked sase-core-rs 0.17.0 wheels. Bumped pyproject.toml and uv.lock to >=0.17.0,<0.18.0, updated the declared-minimum regression expectation, and confirmed a clean --no-sources install resolves the published 0.17.0 wheel and successfully runs 'sase bead show sase-bh' plus 'sase bead ready'. Focused telemetry smoke tests pass (3 passed), full 'just check' passes, and git diff --check is clean.

Verified GitHub/PyPI release v0.17.0, published-wheel task bead and ready-query smoke tests, focused telemetry tests, full just check, and git diff --check; dependency pin and lockfile now require sase-core-rs 0.17.x.
